reviews.title: Fraudulent practices. Predatory marketing.
reviews.text: There is nothing unique about this app that warrants charging money. It is so glitchy that it will kick you out of the app at random. You will have to try multiple times to submit your forms. You will be shown dozens of class actions that you are not eligible for. You will waste more time trying to confirm your eligibility then it would take to find these on your own with Google. Pretty much all of these class actions require you having an email or a letter meaning that you would have already known about this. And the kicker is that their refund policy is created to scam you of your money— they tell you if you haven’t received payment to cover the cost you will be refunded. They don’t tell you that you cannot be eligible until a year passes. They also do not tell you that regardless of the access you give them to your personal email and a lack of eligible class actions, you will be denied your refund for “not doing enough”. Keep in mind that I communicated proactively to understand what was needed to qualify and there is no information provided that I had not already done. Btw, the timeline also falls out of the 3rd party refund policy timeline for Apple and any payment method— intentionally creating a loophole that prevents you from getting your money back.

reviews.title: Not worth it. Save your money
reviews.text: Only rated this 5 stars so it would pop up. I had to pay for a YEARLY subscription to their service before I could even see what I was eligible for & that’s basically nothing for my state. Then they don’t have the actual forms for the class actions on the app.. you still have to click out and go fill the information in every time. And for the ones that have applied to, the app provides NO updates… so I canceled my subscription… now I can no longer login when I’ve previously had no issues.. my subscription works until 02/27 but I can’t login in anymore..? I can’t wait for the class action for this scammy app.  Not to mention the app was for applying to class actions & now all of a sudden they’re changing it to some financial savings app.. y’all baited and switched … we signed up for an app that provides us CLASS ACTION LAWSUITs were eligible for… your company made us pay for a yearly subscription to now change the app… DON’T WASTE YOUR TIME.

reviews.title: MISLEADING & NON REFUNDABLE
reviews.text: Downloaded the app due to the ratings and reviews. Was only presented with a couple options - all said i was eligible. Once getting into it a little bit, it was determined I was not actually eligible and had wasted my time and money. Cancelled my subscription the same night and reached out to inquire about a refund seeing as my expectations were not met, the options given were not actually applicable to me (required living in New York or Las Vegas and I had only used it less than an hour. They let me know that Apple would be responsible for refunding the subscription. Reached out to Apple which is just a whole mess of itself but they denied my claim 2 times and just had a conversation with Neha who yet again did not help me with a single thing. She did let me know that it was automated decision and there was nothing they could do about it. I asked her to specify why the request was being denied and she said she was not able to go into detail about their process and/or how they came to this conclusion. She did send me a link to leave feedback on the experience though! Just reached out to SettleMate again to see if they are willing to give me a refund or not - will update once I know more. I don’t know but as of right now it seems like the perfect scamming partnership is happening between Apple & SettleMate! Please just avoid it as a whole and if you choose not to heed my advice, may it go better for you than it did me!

reviews.title: Cool and easy to understand app, but broken UI functions make it nearly useless
reviews.text: I found the information presented in an easy and digestible format which is nice. It makes it very easy to understand what class actions are available and how relevant they may be to you. This part of the app is pretty great! However, when trying to fill out your birthdate on a form, the calendar format does not allow you to select the year, month, or day manually, you have to tap through each month individually. I was born in 1997… I had to tap the calendar arrow at least 336 times to get to my birth date. After doing so, I accidentally pressed the wrong date and instead of bringing back up the month and year I selected when I tried to correct my mistake, it brought me back to the current calendar date! I stopped filing out the form to write this review, so I will have to tap a button at least 672 times just to fill out a settlement worth $11… yikes! If this feature remains unfixed, I will not be renewing my subscription and cannot rate this application any higher. No matter how useful your application and the data you provide may be, making your UI as cumbersome as this wastes my time and ultimately makes your app useless to me.

reviews.title: Bait & switch and no value
reviews.text:
I watched an ad that featured this app’s users discussing a specific settlement that SettleMate got for them. I downloaded the app that day, from the ad’s link, and that company’s settlement I was seeking was not available. That was incredibly disappointing. It felt like a very misleading ad that can only be described as “bait and switch” IMO. Also, I emailed them that I was charged and I described this scenario and requested a refund. I have not heard back which also makes me think their customer service is not sufficient. I would definitely not recommend this app. I wish I would have read the other reviews before getting charged for a month. 
While the app had other offers, I either was not eligible or I believe it’s highly unlikely that I would expect a settlement payment, so my preference would just be a refund. I don’t think that’s going to happen, but if it did, I would be willing to remove or edit this review. I also see that SettleMate is accusing reviewers of being illegitimate which is not a great look.

reviews.title: Overpriced, spent more than I gained, probably a scam.
reviews.text:
To start, is a very expensive subscription. I wasn’t eligible for any claims through the app. The few that I was eligible for redirected me outside the app to a web browser where I had to fill everything out myself. There was also no guarantee that I would actually receive any money. They also want access to your email and a lot of your personal data, but there is no policy protecting your information. They also don’t tell you if they’re selling your information either. 

It’s incredibly frustrating that the app completely logs you out every time you close it, and there’s no option for FaceID either. When you do log back in again you have to go through all of the intro prompts every time, which ask a bunch of questions about you. It’s a horrible user experience, but maybe that’s intentional so that we forfeit the subscription fee and they don’t have to do any actual work for us.

I have a feeling SettleMate will be in a Settlement in the future…. This app is a complete scam.

reviews.title: Only practical for California users—the actual info you need
reviews.text: This app is really only worth it if you live in California (explanation below). There are generally around 10 or so total claims you are “possibly eligible” to apply for during any given 3+ month period, and usually about 7-8 of these are from obscure companies (e.g. Flo Health), which you will almost certainly not qualify for. The app tries to predict which offers you are eligible for, but it is far less accurate than a coin flip (I did the math). New claims options are rarely added. For the more mainstream companies or companies where you may have a legitimate case, they are almost always for California residents only (sometimes D.C. as well). It’s probably about half of the claims on my app that are restricted to California consumers only. If you live in California and frequently purchase from random companies, it may be worth it. Also, like other reviews have mentioned, the app costs 30 dollars for the year (you can’t pay by month). I can’t remember if that was stated clearly in the app description.

reviews.title: Save Your Money
reviews.text: This app lists current and upcoming class actions. Unfortunately, that's about as much as this app provides you. Most of the class action “matches” the app lists for you are not matches in any way. If you do find a class action suit you meet the requirements for, all the app provides is the information for the company in charge of the settlement. You have to go to a separate site to fill in required information and then wait for an eventual email from a third party to find out what additional documentation you are required to submit. This app doesn't even provide a direct link to the third party, just a long web address you can't even copy/paste to a browser. That is where Settmate’s services end. They provide nothing else. For example, when you return to the app to check on the status of your claim there is zero additional information. Literally nothing. As of today, 6 months in, I have received $0 after multiple submissions. Save your money.

reviews.title: Linking your financial account
reviews.text: They didn’t  show me any new settlements that I didn’t already know about from the class action emails you can subscribe to.   Linking my financial account to find savings didn’t result in anything changing .   The page doesn’t change with any information or suggestions    So I don’t think they do anything with your financial information for your benefit    After linking my account it just says same thing “link your account to find more savings but I’ve already linked the accounts?  I linked email too but it says I’m still missing out because I haven’t linked both.  I hate to complain but it’s like logging into a website and it just takes you to the login page every time

reviews.title: Terrible App, Worse Customer Service
reviews.text:
I never write reviews but my whole experience really irked me. I have been applying to claims left and right for almost a year and have had no luck. Half of the claims that are recommended to you end up taking you outside of the app, so what is the point of the app? I chose to subscribe because of their one year moneyback guarantee that was advertised on their social medias, stating that you’d be refunded if you didn’t make the cost of the subscription back from claims. I think I’ve given them a fair chance and ample time to do that and so I reached out to customer service, who told me to request a refund through the Apple Store. That refund was not possible and they began making excuses as to why it wasn’t possible and stated that I was out of luck and that they couldn’t provide a refund and I’ve wasted my hard earned money. 

Needless to say, I look forward to the inevitable class settlement of Settlemate.
